issue_context.title: kube-scheduler panic on PodAffinity
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

Kube scheduler went into a crash loop after upgrading to 1.15.2. The logs can be located here: https://gist.github.com/bernadinm/30416acf185f4ea36d620d60d81f3f56

```
E0909 23:20:26.016048       1 runtime.go:73] Observed a panic: "invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference" (runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference)
goroutine 366 [running]:
```

We suspect that it is related to this commit here that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/76973/files was introduced in k8s-v1.15.0-alpha


```
kube-scheduler-ip-10-0-1-10             0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   10         5d
kube-scheduler-ip-10-0-2-20             0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   10         5d
kube-scheduler-ip-10-0-3-30             0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   10         4d23h
```

**What you expected to happen**:

This issue was addressed when we downgraded the kube-scheduler to 1.14.6 as this is a supportable skew k8s configuration. 

```
kube-scheduler-ip-10-0-1-10            1/1     Running   20         5d1h
kube-scheduler-ip-10-0-2-20            1/1     Running   20         5d1h
kube-scheduler-ip-10-0-3-30            1/1     Running   20         5d1h
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**Anything else we need to know?**:

We've downgraded the kube-scheduler version from 1.5.2 to 1.14.6.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```

```


comments:
> Another option is to allocate int64 for every node.

We shouldn't do that. That had proved to be a perf regression.

So we should come up with a fix resolving only this issue.

> I am thinking about the following change (looking at the flags inside processPod):

Regarding this approach, isn't `nodeNameToInfo[name].PodsWithAffinity()` designed for pre-processing that?

@bernadinm 
The log snippet you posted contained only the panic.

Are you able to attach / post more of the scheduler log so that we can have more background ?

Thanks
Nvm, I've managed to repro this issue.

This issue has been fixed in the master branch, and will be cherrypicked into v1.15.5 and v1.16.1.

- 1.15 - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82907
- 1.16 - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82902

review_comments: It's intentional to only init the entry when needed because initilizing a `*int64` has overhead - it was captured in the perf tests.

I am looking through current code to see if initialization of the counters misses some case(s).
Proposed another change on the issue.
